head: 99d8932f95cd6dcc0835f02d92edbec9e97e1ad4
description: Frozen acceptance thresholds for the M9 certificate-gated cross-Build TU frontend reuse. The M9 prototype (when implemented) must clear every threshold here against a fresh measurement run on this same HEAD. HARD thresholds are zero-tolerance: a single violation blocks acceptance. Non-HARD thresholds permit bounded slack as documented.

positive_control_target_savings_pct_min.rationale: M8 measured 64.0% theoretical certificate savings on the per-file-config positive-control workload. M9 must deliver >=30% REAL wall-clock savings on that same workload AFTER certificate overhead, to justify production integration. 30% (not 64%) leaves headroom for cert computation and cache-miss paths while still clearing the M8 feasibility bar.

negative_control_max_overhead_pct.rationale: On the FreeRTOS global-config negative-control workload the certificate saves 0% (every L1 unique). M9 must NOT regress that workload's wall-clock by more than 5% — i.e. the certificate gate's no-op overhead must stay cheap. Measured against baseline_negative_control_wall_clock_s.

certificate_cost_per_tu_ms_max.rationale: Certificate computation (L1 key: source hash + config hash + header closure hash) must cost <1ms per TU, so that on the negative-control workload (0 hits) the gate overhead stays well under the 5% regression budget.

frontend_false_reuse_max.rationale: ZERO TOLERANCE. A false frontend reuse is a TU whose real frontend-relevant context differs from a cached entry but the certificate says 'reuse'. M8 proved L1 is a perfect predictor of L2 (0 false-positives in 30 build-pairs). M9 must preserve this: any false reuse is a silent corruption that blocks acceptance.

certificate_false_accept_max.rationale: ZERO TOLERANCE. The certificate must fail CLOSED when equivalence cannot be proven. A false accept (cert says reuse when AST would differ) is a safety violation. Mirrors M8's 0 L1-false-positives guarantee.

gt_parity_failures_max.rationale: ZERO TOLERANCE. Ground-truth parity: the symbols/facts produced by the reuse path must be byte-identical to the symbols/facts produced by the no-reuse path for every reused TU. Any divergence is a correctness failure. M8's AST-fingerprint equality (ba2e9f57... etc.) is the reference ground truth.

baseline_mean_parse_time_per_tu_s.source: baseline_freeze.json summary (50 parses across both workloads)
baseline_mean_parse_time_per_tu_s.drift_note: M9-baseline 0.01632s vs M8 0.0146s. Drift is timing-only (machine/load); AST structure (cursor counts, fingerprints) is bit-identical to M8.

baseline_positive_control_wall_clock_s.source: baseline_freeze.json workload_2 total_wall_s (per-file-config, 25 parses, NO reuse applied)
baseline_positive_control_wall_clock_s.note: This is the no-reuse cost the M9 prototype must beat by >=30% after cert overhead.

baseline_negative_control_wall_clock_s.source: baseline_freeze.json workload_1 total_wall_s (global-config, 25 parses, NO reuse applied)
baseline_negative_control_wall_clock_s.note: Certificate saves 0% here; M9 must not regress this by >5%.

m8_reconfirm_on_head_99d8932.note: All M8 structural/safety measurements re-confirmed bit-identical on HEAD 99d8932. Only absolute timings drifted within machine noise.
